title: Winter Protection Plan Re-Deferral and Good-Faith Payment — Calculation Memo
content:
# Winter Protection Plan Re-Deferral and Good-Faith Payment — Calculation Memo

This memorandum sets the winter re-deferral and the winter good-faith payment when a defaulted Winter Protection Plan, the seasonal kind of Payment Arrangement, is reinstated.

## 1. The returned balance

The winter plan's returned balance is the amount of its latest balance-return entry with reason default — the plan balance that went back onto the service agreement when the plan defaulted.

## 2. The re-deferral and the good-faith payment

- The **winter re-deferral** is the returned balance times one minus the winter good-faith share, rounded half-up to the cent.
- The **winter good-faith payment** is the returned balance less the winter re-deferral, so that the two together make up the returned balance to the cent.

## 3. The winter good-faith share

The combined winter share is the winter missed-installment share plus the winter returned-payment share, added together into one share. The winter good-faith share is the combined winter share, applied once to the returned balance. The standard winter good-faith share is zero, so that the whole returned balance is booked back under the winter plan.

## 4. Review period

As standard, the agreement's returned payments are reviewed over the 12 months before the request. A window of a number of months before the request covers entries dated after the same calendar day that many months earlier, up to and including the request date.

## Worked example (hypothetical winter plan)

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Latest balance-return entry with reason default | $642.18 |
| Winter good-faith share | The standard share of 0 |
| Winter re-deferral | $642.18 times one, rounded half-up to the cent: $642.18 |
| Winter good-faith payment | $642.18 less the re-deferral of $642.18: $0.00 |
| Returned payments reviewed for a request dated January 22 | Those posted after January 22 of the previous year, up to and including January 22 |

**Rounding to the cent (hypothetical good-faith share of 9%).** A returned balance of $642.18 times 0.91 is $584.3838, so the winter re-deferral rounded half-up to the cent is $584.38, and the winter good-faith payment is $642.18 less $584.38, that is $57.80; the two together make up the $642.18.
